question: A ladder is leaning against a wall such that it makes a 45° angle with the ground. If the foot of the ladder is 5 m away from the wall, what is the height of the point (in m) where the ladder touches the wall?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, if the angle of elevation is 45°, the triangle is always isosceles.

This means the perpendicular (height of the wall) and the base (distance from the wall) are strictly equal.

Since the base is given as 5 m, the height at which the ladder touches the wall must also be exactly 5 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• 
• 
 
 45° Base = 5 m h = ? Ladder Wall A B C 

**Given:**

Distance of the foot of the ladder from the wall (Base) = 5 m

Angle of elevation (θ) = 45°

**Formula Used:**

tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ tan(45°) = Height ÷ Base

⇒ 1 = Height ÷ 5

⇒ Height = 5 × 1

⇒ Height = 5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios in Right Triangles

tan(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Base | sin(θ) = Perpendicular ÷ Hypotenuse | cos(θ) = Base ÷ Hypotenuse.

Angles of Elevation and Depression

The angle of elevation is measured upwards from the horizontal line of sight, while the angle of depression is measured downwards. Due to alternate interior angles, they are geometrically equal for the same object.

Pythagorean Theorem

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base². In this scenario, this theorem can be used to find the full length of the ladder once the height and base are known.
